name: How do remodel timelines change when materials are custom or backordered?

mainEntity.name: How do remodel timelines change when materials are custom or backordered?
mainEntity.text: How do remodel timelines change when materials are custom or backordered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Custom and backordered items can affect the critical path of a remodel. If cabinetry, tile, windows, appliances, or specialty fixtures do not arrive on time, work that depends on them may have to pause. That creates idle labor, rescheduling issues, and possible storage or protection challenges. The more custom the project, the more important it is to finalize selections early and confirm lead times before demolition begins. A good contractor should identify long-lead items during planning and explain how they affect the schedule. In luxury Los Angeles remodels, this matters even more because imported materials or custom fabrication can take longer than standard stock products. Homeowners should also ask what happens if a chosen material becomes unavailable and whether acceptable alternates have been preapproved. The best protection is to order critical items early, keep backup options ready, and build schedule buffer into the plan. If materials are still undecided when construction starts, the timeline is much more likely to slip.
acceptedAnswer.description: Custom or backordered materials can delay a remodel by weeks or months because installation often cannot proceed until key items arrive. Long-lead items should be selected and ordered early to protect the schedule.
